paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across nine language families, comparing six model configurations: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The horizontal axis lists the language families in the order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, with no apparent ordering or sorting. The vertical axis on the left represents the effect, labeled with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, marked with ticks at regular intervals of 10, with no units specified. Each model configuration is represented by a distinct color: blue, green, red, and pink, with two shades each. The chart displays grouped bars for each language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. The IE-Indic family shows effects approximately between 17 and 25 across configurations, while Uralic and Isolate show near-zero effects, with bars shorter than 5 across all models. IE-Germanic exhibits effects up to around 20, specifically with XLM-B2, and IE-Slavic shows notably higher effects for B2 variants, with values approximately twice as large as L2 and R2 variants. The Semitic family displays wide error bars, with mBERT-L2 reaching around 15. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color-coded representation, and no specific sorting is applied beyond the ordering of language families.
